answer.rationale: Competitive price-cut pressure on SMB creates immediate churn risk, but exp_73 demonstrated that promotional pricing captures price-sensitive accounts that do not survive renewal—worsening long-term qualified revenue. Instead, memory_44 and the enterprise sales-assist pathway offer a differentiated response: redirect resources toward higher-margin enterprise prospects where demo-request flows show superior pipeline quality and conversion. This shifts the competitive battleground away from unsustainable price competition. Simultaneously, the referral incentive (memory_57) may retain established customers without acquisition cost, but activation and onboarding improvements (memory_31, memory_86, memory_91) are slower and do not address immediate churn. A standard_experiment on enterprise sales assistance preserves the option to layer additional SMB retention tactics (simplified onboarding, activation messaging, referral incentives) once verified, while the primary strategic move is to deepen enterprise wallet share and quality-of-revenue mix rather than match price. This honors the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue over short-term defensive acquisition.
